sections.title: The Intuitive Paradox (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Can a 1D line cover a 2D area?
Topological dimensions challenge our geometric intuition.
Infinite length allows a line to fill space.
Yarn folding visualizes a square tile cover.
Space-filling curves bridge these dimensions perfectly.

Morph the line segment into a 2D square shape. Color: #FF6666.
Animate the recursive filling process of the square. Color: #66FF66.

sections.title: The Recursive Anatomy: Peano & Hilbert (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: Construct curves using recursive divide and conquer.
Split a square into four smaller quadrants.
Connect quadrants to ensure continuous path flow.
Hilbert curves iterate through fractal construction.
Each segment replaces with a smaller shape.
animations: Show Peano axioms representing basic number generation using the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] to illustrate the grid basis. Color: #FF99FF.
Demonstrate the Hilbert curve construction process steps by subdividing the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg]. Color: #99FFFF.
Compare the two curves side by side for structural difference, mapping each path within a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg]. Color: #FF9999.

sections.title: Mathematical Properties: Continuity vs. Differentiability (2:00-3:15)
lecture_lines: These curves remain continuous functions everywhere.
Yet, they are nowhere differentiable curves.
They map intervals onto unit squares perfectly.

Show the trade-off between continuity and differentiability using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg]. Color: #55FF55.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Data Locality (3:15-4:30)
lecture_lines: Space-filling curves preserve crucial spatial locality.
Hilbert search outperforms inefficient row-major scans.

sections.title: Conclusion and Further Exploration (4:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Curves enable efficient data compression techniques.
They optimize pathfinding and image processing.
Drones use these paths for scanning fields.
